2	
3	Carry procedural three.js content into an Aura3D project as a typed asset plus editable Aura3D source, instead of
4	porting it by hand. The bridge carries assets, animation clips, simple shaders, lights, camera and renderer output.
5	Behaviour (input, physics, scoring, UI) stays native Aura3D code. It is a build-time tool: `three` is a dev
6	dependency of your project, never a runtime dependency, and the shipped route imports only `@aura3d/engine`.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing options for the car body rendering—hiding the GLB paint body and rebuilding it natively would duplicate geometry awkwardly, so I'm considering instead baking the flake effect directly into the base color map during export.

Setting metalness and roughness maps to the same texture should work through the exporter's merging path, with flakes getting low roughness/high metalness against a rougher base to create sparkly env reflections through the clearcoat. The pixel-level noise at this resolution will actually read as sparkle aliasing, which works in my favor, so I'm now thinking through the UV repeat scale across the body.

At that density mipmap averaging will wash the flakes out, so I want fewer texels or to disable mipmaps entirely — going with a 128x128 texture, repeat around 5x2.5, and linear filtering with no mipmaps so the aliasing itself produces the shimmer when rotating. I need to check the exporter preserves sampler filter settings, which it does. For the color channels, I'm separating roughness into green and metalness into blue, and considering whether the base color map needs sRGB color space.

Then I'm defining the flake vs non-flake values: flakes get low roughness and full metalness, non-flakes get moderate roughness and lower metalness, with material factors set to 1 so the maps drive everything directly. A normal map could help with glints but I'll skip that for now and move on to editing the recipe.
